title: Phase 5: Protocol and abstract-class design
status_detail: Inactive Phase 5; candidate-specific abstraction children remain deferred until completed module decomposition demonstrates concrete substitution or shared-invariant needs.
objective: Identify and implement only those Protocol, abstract base class, or composition boundaries justified by demonstrated polymorphism, shared invariants, or reusable behavior.
authorized_scope: After accepted prerequisite results and separate activation, examine actual call sites, implementations, substitution requirements, shared state, shared algorithms, lifecycle invariants, and dependency direction for each abstraction candidate.

Prefer concrete composition, use Protocols for structural substitution without shared implementation, and introduce an abstract base class only when nominal identity plus shared invariant or implementation ownership is demonstrated.
Review existing abstractions, including single-implementation bases, and retain, replace, simplify, or remove them according to evidence rather than assuming inheritance is improvement.
Create later candidate-specific descendants only when the exact consumers, implementations, contract, compatibility impact, and verification boundary are known.
completion_criteria: Every inventoried abstraction candidate has a recorded disposition supported by concrete implementations and consumers rather than shared method names alone.
Introduced or retained Protocol and abstract-class contracts are minimal, strictly typed, dependency-correct, documented, and verified through meaningful substitution behavior.
Nominal marker bases, generic DataObject or ActionObject hierarchies, and inheritance used only for code organization are absent from the accepted result.
Applicable source, typing, tests, public imports, documentation, architecture conformance, Harness validation, and projections agree with residual limitations explicit.
exclusions: Do not create a universal DataObject, ResultObject, ActionObject, serializer, validator, repository, Task, or Workflow implementation hierarchy solely for taxonomy.
Do not infer an abstract-class requirement from a common `execute`, `encode`, `decode`, `status`, or identity method without demonstrated substitutability and ownership.
Do not use inheritance to conceal cross-package dependency violations, scientific policy, mutable shared state, or compatibility aliases.
No dependency change, protected execution, release, staging, commit, push, or automatic activation is authorized by this inactive Task.
